title: Universal first order thickenings restrict to open subschemes and do not depend on an open base containing the image
statement: Let $h:Z\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. (0) Let $T\subset T'$ be a first order thickening over $X$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] with closed immersion $i_T:T\to T'$ and structure morphism $b:T'\to X$, let $W'\subseteq T'$ be an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] and $W=i_T^{-1}(W')$. Then $i_T|_W:W\to W'$ is a closed immersion whose ideal sheaf is the restriction to $W'$ of the ideal sheaf of $i_T$, so $W\subset W'$ with $b|_{W'}$ is a first order thickening over $X$; and $W'$ is the only open subscheme of $T'$ with $i_T^{-1}(W')=W$, since $i_T$ is a homeomorphism of underlying spaces. (1) Let $Z\subset Z'$ be a universal first order thickening of $Z$ over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening], with closed immersion $i:Z\to Z'$ and $h':Z'\to X$. Let $V\subseteq Z$ and $U\subseteq X$ be open subschemes with $h(V)\subseteq U$, and let $V'\subseteq Z'$ be the open subscheme with $i^{-1}(V')=V$. Then $h'(V')\subseteq U$, and $V\subset V'$, with closed immersion $i|_V:V\to V'$ and structure morphism $h'|_{V'}:V'\to U$, is a universal first order thickening of $V$ over $U$ (for $h|_V:V\to U$). (2) Let $U\subseteq X$ be an open subscheme with $h(Z)\subseteq U$, write $h_U:Z\to U$ for the factorization of $h$ and $j:U\to X$ for the inclusion. If $Z\subset Z'$, with closed immersion $i$ and $h'_U:Z'\to U$, is a universal first order thickening of $Z$ over $U$ (for $h_U$), then $Z\subset Z'$ with $i$ and $j\circ h'_U:Z'\to X$ is a universal first order thickening of $Z$ over $X$ (for $h$).

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04F3 (lemma-universal-thickening), second paragraph ('We begin with some general remarks': restriction to opens V ⊂ Z, U ⊂ X with h(V) ⊂ U, and 'in a completely similar manner' the change of base from U to X); no tag of its own. Part (0) is the restriction of a thickening to an open used there implicitly

proof.text: *(0), the restriction is a first order thickening over $X$.* Write $j_{W'}:W'\to T'$ and $j_W:W\to T$ for the inclusions (open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion]) and $i_W:=i_T|_W:W\to W'$ for the unique morphism with $j_{W'}\circ i_W=i_T\circ j_W$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] (it exists since $i_T(W)\subseteq W'$, $W$ being $i_T^{-1}(W')$). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-thickening-open-restriction] to the closed immersion $i_T$, the open $W'\subseteq T'$, the structure morphism $b:T'\to X$ and the open $U:=X$ of $X$ (so $b(W')\subseteq X$ trivially and $b|_{W'}=b\circ j_{W'}$ is the factorization it names): $i_W$ is a closed immersion, its ideal sheaf is the restriction $\mathcal I|_{W'}$ of the ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$ of $i_T$, $(\mathcal I|_{W'})^2=0$ since $\mathcal I^2=0$, and $W\subset W'$ with $b|_{W'}$ is a first order thickening over $X$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] (4), $W$ being over $X$ through $b|_{W'}\circ i_W=b\circ j_{W'}\circ i_W=b\circ i_T\circ j_W$, i.e. through the restriction of the structure morphism $b\circ i_T$ of $T$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base].

source.place: Proof of Lemma 04F3 (lemma-universal-thickening), second paragraph ('We begin with some general remarks'): 'Let V' \subset Z' be the open subscheme such that V = Z \cap V''' (used implicitly); Lemma 09ZU (lemma-base-change-thickening) for the base change of a thickening along an open immersion

proof.text: *(0), existence and uniqueness of the open over a given open.* Since $T\subset T'$ is a first order thickening, it is a thickening, so the map of underlying spaces of $i_T$ is a bijective homeomorphism $|T|\to|T'|$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] (1)-(3). Hence for every open $W\subseteq T$ the set $i_T(W)$ is open in $T'$ and is the unique open subset $W'$ with $i_T^{-1}(W')=W$: if $i_T^{-1}(W'_1)=i_T^{-1}(W'_2)$ then $W'_1=i_T(i_T^{-1}(W'_1))=i_T(i_T^{-1}(W'_2))=W'_2$ by surjectivity of $i_T$. An open subscheme of $T'$ is the open subset with the restricted structure sheaf [def-weil-open-immersion], so $W'$ is unique as an open subscheme. In particular, in (1), for $V\subseteq Z$ open there is exactly one open subscheme $V'\subseteq Z'$ with $i^{-1}(V')=V$, namely $V'=i(V)$ as a set, $Z\subset Z'$ being a first order thickening by [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening].

source.place: Proof of Lemma 04F3 (lemma-universal-thickening), second paragraph ('We begin with some general remarks'): 'Let V' \subset Z' be the open subscheme such that V = Z \cap V''; Definition 04EX (definition-thickening)

proof.text: *(1), $V\subset V'$ is a first order thickening over $U$, compatible with $h|_V$.* Write $j_V:V\to Z$, $j_{V'}:V'\to Z'$, $j_U:U\to X$ for the inclusions, $h|_V:V\to U$ for the unique morphism with $j_U\circ h|_V=h\circ j_V$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme], and recall $h'\circ i=h$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening]. By Step 2 every point of $V'$ is $i(v)$ with $v\in V$, and $h'(i(v))=h(v)\in U$; so $h'(V')\subseteq U$, and there is a unique $h'_{V'}:V'\to U$ with $j_U\circ h'_{V'}=h'\circ j_{V'}$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]; this is the morphism $h'|_{V'}:V'\to U$ of the statement. By [lem-weil-pbc-thickening-open-restriction], applied to $i$, $V'$, $h':Z'\to X$ and $U$, the morphism $i_V:=i|_V:V\to V'$ (the unique one with $j_{V'}\circ i_V=i\circ j_V$) is a closed immersion with square-zero ideal sheaf $\mathcal I|_{V'}$ and $V\subset V'$ is a first order thickening over $U$ through $h'_{V'}$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. It is a thickening of $V$ over $U$ for the given $h|_V$: $j_U\circ h'_{V'}\circ i_V=h'\circ j_{V'}\circ i_V=h'\circ i\circ j_V=h\circ j_V=j_U\circ h|_V$, so $h'_{V'}\circ i_V=h|_V$ by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] (applied to the morphism $h\circ j_V:V\to X$, whose image lies in $U$).

source.place: Proof of Lemma 04F3 (lemma-universal-thickening), second paragraph ('We begin with some general remarks'): 'Let V' \subset Z' be the open subscheme such that V = Z \cap V'. Then we claim that V \subset V' is the universal first order thickening of V over U'

proof.text: *(1), existence of the morphism of thickenings.* Let $T\subset T'$ be a first order thickening over $U$, with closed immersion $i_T:T\to T'$ and structure morphism $b:T'\to U$, and let $a:T\to V$ with $h|_V\circ a=b\circ i_T$. Then $T\subset T'$ with $j_U\circ b:T'\to X$ is a first order thickening over $X$ (the closed immersion and its ideal sheaf are unchanged; $T$ is over $X$ through $j_U\circ b\circ i_T$) [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], [def-weil-scheme-over-base], and $j_V\circ a:T\to Z$ satisfies $h\circ j_V\circ a=j_U\circ h|_V\circ a=(j_U\circ b)\circ i_T$. By the universal property of $Z\subset Z'$ over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening] there is a unique $a'':T'\to Z'$ with $h'\circ a''=j_U\circ b$ and $a''\circ i_T=i\circ j_V\circ a$. The map $i_T$ is surjective on underlying spaces ($T\subset T'$ is a thickening, [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] (1)-(3)), so every point of $T'$ is $i_T(t)$, and $a''(i_T(t))=i(j_V(a(t)))\in i(V)=V'$ (Step 2); hence $a''(T')\subseteq V'$ and there is a unique $a':T'\to V'$ with $j_{V'}\circ a'=a''$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. It is a morphism of thickenings over $U$: $j_U\circ h'_{V'}\circ a'=h'\circ j_{V'}\circ a'=h'\circ a''=j_U\circ b$, so $h'_{V'}\circ a'=b$; and $j_{V'}\circ a'\circ i_T=a''\circ i_T=i\circ j_V\circ a=j_{V'}\circ i_V\circ a$, so $a'\circ i_T=i_V\circ a$; both cancellations of $j_U$, resp. $j_{V'}$, are the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] (two morphisms into the open subscheme whose composites with the inclusion agree are both the unique factorization of that composite).

source.place: Proof of Lemma 04F3 (lemma-universal-thickening), second paragraph ('We begin with some general remarks'): 'By the universal property of Z' we obtain (a, a') : (T \subset T') \to (Z \subset Z'). But since we have equality |T| = |T'| of underlying topological spaces we see that a'(T') \subset V'. Hence we may think of (a, a') as a morphism of thickenings (a, a') : (T \subset T') \to (V \subset V') over U'

proof.text: *(1), uniqueness; conclusion of (1).* In the situation of Step 4, let $a'_1,a'_2:T'\to V'$ both satisfy $h'_{V'}\circ a'_k=b$ and $a'_k\circ i_T=i_V\circ a$. Then $j_{V'}\circ a'_k:T'\to Z'$ satisfies $h'\circ j_{V'}\circ a'_k=j_U\circ h'_{V'}\circ a'_k=j_U\circ b$ and $j_{V'}\circ a'_k\circ i_T=j_{V'}\circ i_V\circ a=i\circ j_V\circ a$, so $j_{V'}\circ a'_1=j_{V'}\circ a'_2$ by the uniqueness in the universal property of $Z\subset Z'$ over $X$ applied as in Step 4 [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening], and $a'_1=a'_2$ by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. With Steps 3 and 4, $V\subset V'$ with $i_V$ and $h'_{V'}$ is a universal first order thickening of $V$ over $U$ for $h|_V$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening].

source.place: Proof of Lemma 04F3 (lemma-universal-thickening), second paragraph ('We begin with some general remarks'): 'Uniqueness is clear also'

proof.text: *(2), $Z\subset Z'$ is a first order thickening over $X$.* The closed immersion $i:Z\to Z'$ and its square-zero ideal sheaf do not depend on the base; $Z'$ is over $X$ through $j\circ h'_U$, and $(j\circ h'_U)\circ i=j\circ h_U=h$ since $h'_U\circ i=h_U$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening]. So $Z\subset Z'$ is a first order thickening of $Z$ over $X$ for $h$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] (4), [def-weil-scheme-over-base].

source.place: Proof of Lemma 04F3 (lemma-universal-thickening), second paragraph ('We begin with some general remarks'): 'In a completely similar manner one proves that if h(Z) \subset U and Z \subset Z' is a universal first order thickening over U, then Z \subset Z' is a universal first order thickening over X'

proof.text: *(2), existence.* Let $T\subset T'$ be a first order thickening over $X$, with closed immersion $i_T$ and structure morphism $b:T'\to X$, and $a:T\to Z$ with $h\circ a=b\circ i_T$. Every point of $T'$ is $i_T(t)$ with $t\in T$ ($i_T$ is surjective, [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] (1)-(3)), and $b(i_T(t))=h(a(t))\in h(Z)\subseteq U$; so $b(T')\subseteq U$ and there is a unique $b_U:T'\to U$ with $j\circ b_U=b$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. Thus $T\subset T'$ with $b_U$ is a first order thickening over $U$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] (4), and $h_U\circ a=b_U\circ i_T$, because $j\circ h_U\circ a=h\circ a=b\circ i_T=j\circ b_U\circ i_T$ and both $h_U\circ a$ and $b_U\circ i_T$ are then the unique factorization of $h\circ a$ through $U$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. By the universal property of $Z\subset Z'$ over $U$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening] there is a (unique) $a':T'\to Z'$ with $h'_U\circ a'=b_U$ and $a'\circ i_T=i\circ a$; then $(j\circ h'_U)\circ a'=j\circ b_U=b$, so $a'$ is a morphism of thickenings over $X$ as required.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 04F3 (lemma-universal-thickening), second paragraph ('We begin with some general remarks'): 'In a completely similar manner one proves ...' (the argument of the first claim, with |T| = |T'| used to see that T' maps into U)

proof.text: *(2), uniqueness; conclusion of (2).* In the situation of Step 7, if $a'':T'\to Z'$ satisfies $j\circ h'_U\circ a''=b$ and $a''\circ i_T=i\circ a$, then $h'_U\circ a''$ and $b_U$ are both morphisms $T'\to U$ whose composite with $j$ is $b$, so $h'_U\circ a''=b_U$ by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme], and $a''=a'$ by the uniqueness in the universal property of $Z\subset Z'$ over $U$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening]. With Steps 6 and 7, $Z\subset Z'$ with $i$ and $j\circ h'_U$ is a universal first order thickening of $Z$ over $X$ for $h$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening].

split_report.summary: Split along the second paragraph of the proof of Stacks 04F3 (more-morphisms.tex, lemma-universal-thickening). Eight steps: (0) restriction of a first order thickening to an open W' of T' via the existing Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-thickening-open-restriction (with U = X), and existence/uniqueness of the open W' over a given open of T from the homeomorphism |T| = |T'| of def-sbc-first-order-thickening; (1) h'(V') in U from the points of V' being i(V), V in V' a first order thickening over U compatible with h|_V (thickening-open-restriction, morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme), existence of the dotted arrow from the universal property of Z' over X and |T| = |T'|, uniqueness by cancelling the open immersion j_{V'} (uniqueness clause of lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme); (2) T' maps into U since |T| = |T'| and h(Z) in U, so the thickening is over U and the universal property over U applies, uniqueness by cancelling j. No new node: every non-elementary fact is an existing node (the two Mathlib leaves above, the definitions). Statement and stmt_deps kept. The proof is the general (not formally unramified) form of Steps 2-4 of lem-weil-pbc-universal-thickening-open-restriction; formal unramifiedness of h is used nowhere.

reviewed.note: 8 steps following the second paragraph of the proof of 04F3: (0) by the thickening-open-restriction leaf with U = X and the uniqueness of the open over a given open (i_T a homeomorphism); (1) h'(V') in U on points, V in V' a thickening over U by the same leaf, existence through the universal property over X and factorization through V' (points) and through U (cancelling open immersions by the factoring leaf), uniqueness likewise; (2) the base change from U to X: b factors through U on points, then the universal property over U. Statement unchanged. Stage-3 note: lem-weil-pbc-universal-thickening-open-restriction (04FA) proves (1) again under a superfluous formally-unramified hypothesis.
